extracted.intended_audience: general encyclopedia readers and fans of Mary Higgins Clark (also useful to aspiring suspense writers)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biographical article summarizing the life, career, works, and reception of suspense novelist Mary Higgins Clark. Includes incidental craft notes and anecdotes about her writing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise writing that advances plot every paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: “Fitting an entire sketch into four minutes taught Higgins Clark how to write cleanly and succinctly, traits that are incredibly important to a suspense novel, which must advance the plot with every paragraph.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy of prose is essential in suspense: every paragraph should move the plot forward. Practice that enforces strict length/time limits (e.g., four-minute radio sketches) can train an author to remove extraneous material and keep narrative momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate plot ideas from newspapers and 'what if' prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Her NYU professor told the class they should develop plot ideas by reading newspapers and asking themselves prompts such as, 'Suppose...?' and 'What if...?' She has said that she still gets many of her ideas by utilizing said prompts, along with 'Why?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current events and provocative open-ended questions ('Suppose...?', 'What if...?', 'Why?') as deliberate prompts to seed plots and plot twists. Regularly scan news sources for real-world hooks that can be dramatized with a speculative question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured peer workshop critique (time-limited feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: The workshop met weekly. At each meeting two members would have twenty minutes each to present their latest work. The other members would then have three minutes each to offer constructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use disciplined, time-boxed workshops: short presentations followed by brief, focused constructive comments from peers. This enforces concision in presentation and concentrates feedback, making critique sessions efficient and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe real conversations and environments for material
rubrics_metrics.description: She worked as a switchboard operator... where she often listened in to the residents' conversations. In her memoir she recalls spending much time eavesdropping on Tennessee Williams...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather authentic dialogue, character details, and scene ideas by attentive observation of everyday conversations and settings. Translating real speech patterns and situations into fiction can lend realism and specificity to characters and scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use personal experience and research to inform fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: For her first NYU writing assignment she used this method to expand her own experiences into a short story called 'Stowaway'... Using her research and experience with the Portraits of a Patriot series, Higgins Clark spent the next three years writing a fictionalized account of the relationship between George and Martha Washington.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine personal experience with targeted research to create believable plots and details. Memoir material, workplace experience, or research projects can be fictionalized or adapted into central story elements to increase authenticity and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain genre-appropriate tone (audience/critical expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: She wrote several Christmas-themed mystery novels with her daughter. Although popular with readers, some critics have complained that the books are of lesser quality because the tone is much lighter than her solo output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that shifts in tone (e.g., lighter/holiday tone vs. traditional suspense) can change critical reception and reader expectations. When collaborating or experimenting with subgenres, consider how tonal changes affect perceived quality within the target genre.
